title: Jurisdiction
description: A governed territory: a country, region, municipality, or special-purpose area.

@type.description: A `Jurisdiction` is a `Place`. It has no employees, departments, or legislation - those belong to the `Organization` that governs it, which points here with `areaServed`. Keeping these two apart is the central rule of this profile. Use the most specific schema.org type below that applies.

alternateName.description: Endonyms, historical names, and the local-language term for the tier (e.g. 'Comune di Bologna').

description.description: A plain-language description of the jurisdiction.

url.description: Where more information about this jurisdiction can be found.

identifier.description: At least one. A Wikidata QID is strongly recommended as the cross-border join key.

sameAs.description: Links to authoritative external records for this jurisdiction, e.g. its Wikidata entry.

containedInPlace.description: The next jurisdiction up. Chaining these yields the full territorial hierarchy without any country-specific nesting rules.

containsPlace.description: Jurisdictions directly contained within this one.

population.description: A QuantitativeValue, so the count keeps its observation date and source.

jurisdictionOf.description: `GovernmentOrganization`s governing this area. Convenience inverse of `Organization.areaServed`.

boundary.description: References to `Boundary` entities for this area, including superseded ones. Separate entities rather than inline geometry so that a historical extent can be cited: an electoral district boundary is exactly what gets cited in a dispute, and a citation needs something to point at.
